He can go well with the stiff uphill finish expected to suit, but BAY CITY ROLLER could have their measure. Unbeaten after three starts including winning the Group 2 Champagne Stakes at Doncaster, he drops in class for his return to action and could be up to giving 5lb and a beating to the rest of the field.

selections.comment: Having won two of his last three starts and seemingly thriving on being kept busy, CROWD QUAKE is very hard to oppose. Being by Dubawi and out of the high-class Summer Romance - a Group 2 winner for Charlie Appleby - there is an awful lot to like about this Godolphin home-bred colt. On The Inlet, who cost 160,000gns and is a full-brother to Hungerford Stakes winner Jumby, also captures the imagination. selections.comment: A drop back to a sprint trip worked the oracle for NEZEEH at Cork and that gives him every chance in this claimer. Dylan O'Connor's 10lb claim eases the joint top-weight's burden and leaves him nicely weighted against his rivals. Devil's Angel is another recent winner who enters the equation. He beat a big field at Navan and is well drawn in stall one. Colin Keane is a notable booking for Lismacbryan Hill, who should be monitored for market strength. I Bid You Ajou has snippets of form that entitle him to respect in this company.

selections.comment: SAPPHIRE PRINCESS has shown more than enough to suggest that a maiden should soon be within her grasp. The Kingman filly has been placed in both maidens she has contested in Cork and the form looks strong. The horse who beat her into second on debut has since been placed in a Group 3, while the winner of her latest race went on to be fifth in the Irish 1,000 Guineas last weekend. Sun Soldier offered plenty to work with when a promising second on debut behind the favourite in a Navan maiden, while Gypsy Queen came home a never-nearer fifth on her first outing in Limerick and should improve upon that result.

She certainly knows where the winning post is having landed three of her previous five races, and Billy Lee comes in for the ride for the first time. No Return was just over a length behind her in fourth in that Naas sprint. He gets first-time cheekpieces and can go well. Misappropriation didn't show her true colours on her seasonal reappearance at the Curragh, but could bounce back under a promising 7lb claimer. Red Veil makes her handicap debut off a long absence and shouldn't be a back-marker.

Navorrosse showed that her next turn may not be far away when placed in Navan and Gowran Park.

He usually races prominently so Jamie Powell will need to get him away well from stall 16. Northern Attitude showed a lot more in second on her handicap debut at Roscommon and the blinkers that were deployed there are retained. Great Mover could be a factor after a couple of placed efforts over further last season. Spent All Me Money was a ready winner of a claiming maiden in Roscommon, which has earned him top weight on his first venture into a handicap.

selections.comment: Sea The Stars filly STEP TO SOMEWHERE kept on without threatening in third at Navan last month and can improve upon that. It was her seasonal reappearance and winners have come out of the race. Breathe Again posted her best result to date when third over an extended 1m1f at Gowran Park and there could be more to come from Sheila Lavery's charge, while Alto Sax won a claimer over C&D a year ago and ran well in second when last seen over 1m in Leopardstown. Rockbury Lad finished behind him in fifth there, but has ability and won on his penultimate appearance in Bellewstown. He looks well worth another go at this trip.

selections.comment: FLYING FORTRESS was professional when winning on stable debut at Ballinrobe and could go in again. He showed ability in Britain when trained by James Owen as he finished runner-up on two occasions at Yarmouth. Winston Junior is a horse to note making his handicap bow. He has attracted support in three maiden outings, with best finishes of fifth at Galway and the Curragh. He competes off a mark of 71 with Keithen Kennedy's 5lb claim factored in. A step up in trip and a drop into claiming company, with first-time cheekpieces, saw Fantazy Man take the spoils in Ballinrobe. He has to give weight away, but that was a solid performance and he could be progressive.

Ifallgoeswell disappointed at Killarney earlier this month and while he had previously shown form, he has been frustrating to follow. Couldntmakeitup was well beaten by the winner when finishing second at Kilbeggan recently and needs to improve.

selections.comment: KEEP UP has shown good ability in bumpers and will be ready on jumps debut. From a useful French family, she defeated a subsequent winner on her Roscommon introduction last August and while then beaten 16 lengths into fifth at Listed level in October, that Gowran race was smart and she finished a long way ahead of the other runners. One of those was Cameletta Vega, who earlier this month defeated Emily Love to score at Cork. Emily Love has recent hurdling form, though, which is a big help, but lacks the selection's ability. Galway Festival bumper winner Fortunate Lighting failed to recover after being badly hampered at Wexford and is capable of better.

Faceman, out of top racemare Solerina, debuts in handicaps on his first run since December. The Striker Dylan flopped on a recent Sligo reappearance, but has proven form at this level and now wears first-time cheekpieces.

A half-brother to four winners, including a German Group 3 scorer, he was well beaten in three maiden hurdles but showed promise at Fairyhouse in April before tasting success at Down Royal 24 days ago. He is 7lb higher, but defeated plenty of rivals and is well suited by a sound surface. Tir Og has recent form and while the selection has stronger credentials, she is just a four-year-old so can continue to improve. Hob's Angel hung left when showing improvement at Tramore last month, but is nonetheless an exposed 12-race maiden.

The Getaway mare did well to score over an extended two miles around Tramore and should appreciate going a bit further now. A mark of 110 doesn't look harsh as there is scope for a bit more improvement from her. Shadow Paddy also comes here in winning form and has to be respected. He left previous form well behind at Tipperary just over two weeks ago and got an 8lb hike for that victory. Rut Daniels, an easy winner of a maiden hurdle here back in November, is another relatively unexposed sort who has to be on the shortlist.

selections.comment: Stepping up in trip may help the well-bred JEKIKI and there looks to be a race in her off this kind of mark. The Soldier Of Fortune mare, who is out of a half-sister to Jezki, showed up better at Clonmel last time when plugging on to finish fifth and stretches out over a couple of furlongs further now. It's Time Again was a game winner at Ballinrobe on her return to action last month and is entitled to play a big part again after just a 5lb rise. Kiln Time is consistent at a low level and could be one for a place.

First Company has been seen to best effect on AW with his last three wins coming at Kempton, but rarely tried on turf and has dropped to a workable mark.

selections.comment: Some real potential future high-class handicappers here, well backed last time The King's Falcon was unlucky not to win when not getting a clear run at Epsom, pulling clear of the remainder of the field. Debut winner Push The Limit was just held in a good effort giving weight to the winner at Newmarket last time, he's dropped back in trip to his winning debut distance again. DANGER BAY impressed on debut in a good little race up against more experienced rivals, 1/2l off Hawksbill who has been pitched at Group level, he's been off since August but should be expected to improve for that effort and that looks the strongest form here.

selections.comment: Queensland Boy has obvious claims after bouncing back from a poor spell and with conditions set right looks to hold the strongest cards. The worry is that the son of Australia has rarely put two good runs together in the last couple of years and at likely cramped odds it may be worth looking elsewhere. Smith made a very encouraging return to the Flat over course and distance in late April having landed a similar event to this here in December and could be the one again but a chance is taken that SYDNEY SEABREEZE can leave a disappointing run behind him last time, when sent off favourite, and replicate the course and distance run last September when beaten just 1.5l into fourth off a mark of 65. He now races off 59 and could represent a bit of value. The consistent Balgowan also needs considering

selections.comment: This looks a straight forward task for BORN RULER, on paper at least. Not quite at his best last time when 4th of ten in a class 2 handicap better can be expected here eased markedly in grade. He should be tought to beat. Prometeo is best placed to serve it up to the selection having shown progression late last term to land a hat-trick. His return to action was encouraging enough and if taking another step forward can go close. Rogue Soldier has serious questions to answer after two dismal efforts this term (both at 7f) but has a decent opportunity in this weak affair to bounce back now tackling a more appropriate trip and can make his presence felt. Encourager, returning from a very lengthy absence is probably best watched but certainly had the ability to get competitive in a race like this when last seen in October 2023 and can't be dismissed

selections.comment: EL BUDOOR may have been seventh of 10 on her debut, but she was only beaten about five lengths and was in a good race at Ascot. She should improve markedly for that experience and can go close this time. Miss Herschel is clearly a contender having run well herself on her only start, but seemed to know what she was about and probably has less room for improvement than the selection. She is also making her seasonal debut. Third home could be Cloaks Of Gold who was weak in the betting having had a wind operation before her first start, but ran well regardless, should improve and be in the shake-up.

Rogue Endeavour was a length or so in front of the selection at Salisbury and is actually a bit better off but doesn't appear to have quite the same potential for improvement. That said, he's no doubt entitled to go close. Bluesy Moon heads the list of dangers. He showed a bit of versatility in running style last time, leading the way, and can get involved along with Castellina who made an encouraging return to action and has plenty of scope for improvement

selections.comment: A trappy affair with many in with a chance on the pick of their form. PADISHAKH looks the most solid arriving in top order with a win over a mile back in the UK after a decent stint in Meydan. The trip is a slight query but he wasn't beaten far his only try at it when in Meydan recently (5th of 15, beaten under 4l at 50/1) and he won over 9f when trained in France. Ed Bethell's charge has shown versatility ground-wise and off just a 3lb rise can go close again. One that might be overlooked in the market but could go very well is High Point, who could take a big leap forward back on turf. His AW form reads 4677 where as he's won three of his six turf runs. Soft ground is probably ideal but he won on good ground over this trip at Windsor off a 2lb lower mark early in his career. He can chase the selection home ahead of Arthur's Realm, Let's Dream and Fincancer

selections.comment: TICKETS has a good opportunity to land a double having hit form returned to turf off a much lower mark than for the AW. Certainy on balance his AW form is better but the pick of his turf form is not too far below it and the manner of his win at Redcar suggests a 4lb rise may not be enough to halt the momentum. Juryman, in first time cheekpieces, is feared most. He left his disappointing seasonal bow well behind when dropped to this trip and staying on to get within a length of the winner a few weeks back. He's pretty unexposed at 6f still and can exploit a rails draw to track the pace before being delivered late. With luck in running he'll go close. Variety Island and Ishe Worth Agamble have claims but Hurstwood, who improved dramatically back on turf last time and has a decent record here, is fancied to make the frame

selections.comment: In a race where the only horse with experience on the track needs to step up markedly from debut, this can fall to one of a clutch of interesting newcomers. Top of that list is MAN OF VISION. The Charlie Appleby yard have won three of the last five runnings of this race, boast a 57 per cent strike-rate with their juveniles this season, and, as you would expect from Godolphin, is bred in the purple. Rodeo also represents powerful connections. This homebred colt ticks plenty of boxes on pedigree and could well be up to winning on debut, albeit the yard's runners can come on for a run. On The Inlet is marginally preferred to Velocity Vow. The former is an expensive purchase and the yard have sent out two winning juvenile debutants this year, including for this owner, while the latter is another pricey colt hailing from a yard that won the race in 2023 and can have their runners hard-boiled on debut.

selections.comment: While SHOWERING has a 7lb penalty to carry for his debut success on this seasonal return and turf debut, the colt was second next time out behind a heavily-backed debutant who then subsequently scored decisively under a penalty on his 3yo reappearance, and was thought good enough to take his chance in the Craven Stakes (Gr3) following that, albeit finishing last at Newmarket. Representing William Haggas, the top course trainer, Showering has the potential to rate higher as his full-brother was a dual Class 2 handicap winner over 6f/7f. Miss Cartesian, also on turf debut, is the standout danger to the selection. An odds-on winner at Wolverhampton on debut in November, the filly won despite running green early. She returns here under a winner's penalty for her in-form trainer, and while entitled to improve on second start in receipt of her 5lb sex allowance, there is just a doubt about the quality of opposition she beat on that debut as there have been no subsequent winners to come out of that contest. Atmosphere improved from debut when a keeping-on fifth after being denied a clear run at Kempton last time out, but, while entitled to come on again for that, has plenty to find with the two principals.

selections.comment: SHOW BIZ KID was suited by the step up in trip when scoring by a neck over C&D off 70 on his penultimate start. Although beaten at Pontefract off a 2lb rise last time, that race was run at a crawl and this lightly raced consistent performer can regain the winning thread off a 3lb higher mark off a likely stronger pace in this bigger field. Sir Edward Lear should be sharper for his close-up second at Windsor on seasonal return, had excuses for his soft-ground defeat off an absence before that and this lightly-raced gelding is a leading contender for his in-form trainer. Charming Whisper was below form when down the field over 8f at Newmarket last time out, but is usually consistent, goes well here, acts on the ground, and, with a top jockey back on board, will suit this class drop after racing in 21k and 18k contests the last twice.

selections.comment: SPINNING WHEEL stayed on nicely to make a winning debut over 10f at Beverley and can defy a penalty to score again up in trip. The gelding's pedigree suggests this extended 11f will suit and, with two of those behind him in Yorkshire scoring subsequently, the form looks solid. There were excuses for Marnier when a beaten favourite on his second start when rushed up wide after a slow gate before weakening into fourth in a 10f maiden at Chester last time. It would be no surprise to see an improved effort from this big colt dropped down in class on a more suitable track for his in-form yard. Caughtredhanded was well below the form of his Wood Ditton debut when down the field in a 10f maiden at Newbury last time out and looks the yard's second string, but this Cracksman colt is bred to suit the step up in trip and could well post an improved performance fitted with a first-time-visor.

He is rated 39lb lower than when in his pomp in the UK and proved he retained some of his ability when runner up last time. He did much the best of those forcing the pace that day and the form if working out very well. Consistent dual purpose performer Phoenix Cowboy can lead home the remainder.
